senses.definition: To make a bad situation worse.
senses.caution: It assigns blame, so saying a decision exacerbated an outage sounds like an accusation. Use it only for making something bad worse, never for growth or demand.
senses.example: The retry logic did not cause the outage, but it exacerbated it. We hammered a service that was already on its knees.

cues.text: In a post-incident review you need to say that an automatic retry turned a small failure into a two-hour one, without putting it on the person who wrote it.
A hiring freeze meant to save money has made the delivery backlog worse, and you are explaining that to the sponsor who ordered the freeze.
Your neighbour's fix for the damp has trapped more water in the wall than there was before.
A friend keeps looking at their ex's photos and cannot understand why each week is harder than the one before.

distractors: To put right what went wrong.
To back a claim with evidence someone else can check.
To keep at something long after most people would stop.
To make something deliberately hard to understand.
